hard_case: the changed call is the branch of a braceless `if` in an owner with a nested function; rule 1 must place the branch directly in the owner body, outside the callback

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: `send` is called with `charged 360 cents` instead of `charged 360`

reasoning: `chargeBraceless` sums with a `reduce` callback and calls `notifier.send(owner, "charged " + total)` as the branch of a braceless `if (total > 0)`; the edit appends ` cents`. The test passes `{ send }` and pins `expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledWith("ann", "charged 360")`, which fails. RIPR-SPEC-0256 example 4 (amended 2026-10-15): rule 1 accepts the changed line as the branch of a braceless `if` whose `if` starts a statement directly in the owner body, so the branch runs at most once per owner call and the nested `reduce` callback cannot run it. ripr credits the payload as mock_expectation / strong and reads `exposed`, matching the discriminated truth.
